name: Haiku small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Rotated small/mid-cap cloud/AI/fintech with reduced tech leverage and raised cash; tactical trim of most-pressured positions (MDB, CRWD, DDOG) and rebalance toward fintech strength (SOFI, UPST) amid rising-yield environment.
reassessment_note: Macro backdrop shifted meaningfully this week: 10-year Treasury yields spiked to 4.80% (highest since Jan 2025), Fed Warsh signaling hawkish stance on inflation, and hot jobs report Friday triggering risk-off tape. Cloud/software sector pressure evident in DDOG (-10.17%), CRWD (-7.75%), MDB (-18.67%) losses despite intact fundamentals. Rising yields pressure high-duration tech/SaaS valuations, requiring defensive rebalance. Elected to trim most-pressured positions (MDB 6.66%→1%, CRWD 8.51%→5%, DDOG 7.6%→4%) and raise cash from 15% to 30% for dry powder. Fintech plays (SOFI, UPST) showing relative strength with less rate sensitivity; increased SOFI 8%→10% and UPST 3%→5%. Maintained core small/mid-cap mandate via ARKK, IWM, TQQQ with protective 12% stops. Book rotated from 85% gross exposure to 70% for improved risk-adjusted positioning.

positions.thesis: ARK Innovation ETF remains core small/mid-cap growth holding with concentrated tech/AI/disruptive exposure; outperformed this week (+0.76%) and retains conviction through volatility. Slight trim from 16% reflects macro caution but position remains meaningful for mandate.

Russell 2000 provides broad small-cap diversification; up 20% YTD. Trimmed 1% from 15% given GuruFocus signal of 51% overvaluation vs. intrinsic value. Retains core weighting but reduced sizing reflects tail risk from Fed tightening.

3x leveraged Nasdaq ETF provides tech upside leverage but leverage itself creates risk in rising-rate environment where duration matters. Trimmed from 10% to 8% to reduce portfolio volatility and rate-shock exposure while maintaining tactical leverage.

SoFi showing relative strength (+1.90% this week) and Wall Street bullish reset (Scotiabank Outperform, $25 target vs. current ~$18). Fintech capital-light model less rate-sensitive than cloud SaaS; Kraken deal strengthens crypto/fintech positioning. Increased from 8% to 10%.

CrowdStrike quality cybersecurity play with strong Q2 results, but trimmed 3.5% from 8.51% to reduce concentration risk and take partial profits from earlier rally. Sector rotation pressure and yield sensitivity warrant lighter exposure; FalCon 2026 innovation pipeline justifies retention.

Datadog quality SaaS infrastructure play down 10.17% this week on profit-taking and yield shock. Fundamentals intact but trimmed from 7.6% to 4% to reduce software sector concentration; will reassess if valuations normalize post-rate-shock.

MongoDB hit hardest (-18.67%) this week; valuation stretch evident. Trimmed dramatically from 6.66% to 1% to free capital for higher-conviction trades and reduce tech database concentration. Token position maintains database-tech exposure while protecting downside.

Shopify reported strong Q1 GMV (+35% YoY) but stock pressured by LLM cost concerns and agentic-commerce skepticism. Trimmed 0.7% to 5%; position retains e-commerce secular growth exposure while acknowledging near-term headline risk.

Upstart fintech lending down 2.2% but faces mean-reversion bounce opportunity if macro clarity improves. Capital-light AI lending model attractive with rates stabilizing. Increased from 3% to 5% to capture beaten-down fintech valuations; mean-reversion opportunity in lending.

Snowflake data-cloud play up +1.73% this week, showing sector resilience despite software pressure. Light trim to 3% from 2.85% maintains exposure; earnings looming could drive volatility but long-term AI data infrastructure thesis remains sound.
